data.subject: USDA Chief Information Officers Council
data.opi: Office of the Chief Information Officer
data.scope: This policy applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, and contractors working for, or on behalf of, USDA.
data.purpose: This Departmental Regulation (DR) maintains the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Chief Information Officers (CIO) Council as a permanently chartered committee. This DR defines the CIO Council’s scope, authority, membership, and voting guidelines.
policy_actors: Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General
Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_obligations: The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on the technical and managerial soundness of the Department’s IT initiatives, policies, procedures, and standards.

The CIO Council identifies opportunities to share information resources, assesses the needs of the Department’s IT workforce, serves as a focal point for coordinating responses to Departmentwide IT challenges, and partners with other governmental councils to address issues and risks that require multidisciplinary and multilevel solutions.
The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments.
IT initiatives that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives will remain subject to, and will conform to, DR 3130-010 throughout their life cycle.
The USDA CIO will preside over the CIO Council, appoint the OCIO Executive Secretariat, and serve as a voting member.
The Deputy CIO will serve as a CIO Council voting member.
Mission Area Assistant CIOs will serve as CIO Council voting members.
The Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General, will serve as a CIO Council voting member.
Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO) will serve as CIO Council advisory (non-voting) members.
OCIO Division Officers will serve as CIO Council advisory (non-voting) members.
The OCIO Executive Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve as a CIO Council advisory (non-voting) member.
obligation_conditions: IT matters may become IT investments as defined by DR 3130-013.
The CIO Council designates an IT initiative as an enterprise initiative.
The OCIO Executive Secretariat serves as an advisory (non-voting) member when appointed by the USDA CIO.

policy_statements.text: The CIO Council’s bylaws set out the operating procedures of the CIO Council. A current copy of these bylaws, Bylaws of the United States Department of Agriculture Chief Information Officers Council, appears on the CIO Council’s shared site.
This DR maintains the USDA CIO Council under the authority of:
The CIO Council serves as one of the principal USDA IT advisory forums of the USDA CIO. Its purpose is to improve the operational efficiency and strategic use of IT across the USDA enterprise.
The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on the technical and managerial soundness of the Department’s IT initiatives, policies, procedures, and standards.

The CIO Council identifies opportunities to share information resources. It assesses the needs of the Department’s IT workforce. It serves as a focal point for coordinating responses to Departmentwide IT challenges. It partners with other governmental councils to address issues and risks that require multidisciplinary and multilevel solutions.
policy_statements.target: Information resources, Department’s IT workforce, Departmentwide IT challenges, and issues and risks requiring multidisciplinary and multilevel solutions

policy_statements.text: The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments, as defined by DR 3130-013, Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control. IT initiatives that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives will remain subject to, and will conform to, DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance, throughout their life cycle.
policy_statements.target: IT matters and IT initiatives designated as enterprise initiatives
conditions: IT matters may become IT investments as defined by DR 3130-013.
The CIO Council designates an IT initiative as an enterprise initiative.
policy_statements.classification_result: An IT initiative designated by the CIO Council as an enterprise initiative.
consequences: The initiative remains subject to and conforms to DR 3130-010 throughout its life cycle.
